proof:
Conventions. λ is Lebesgue measure on ℝ. ∫_{(σ,ρ]} denotes the integral over Ioc σ ρ, and ∫_σ^ρ denotes the interval integral. Put F(t) := I(t)/tⁿ and D(τ) := J₁(τ)/τⁿ + L(τ)/τⁿ⁺¹.

1. (Positivity.) Every τ ∈ [σ, ρ] satisfies τ ≥ σ > 0, so τ^m ≠ 0 for every m ∈ ℕ.

2. (Quotient rule.) Fix τ ∈ [σ, ρ]. I has derivative I₁(τ) at τ, the map t ↦ tⁿ has derivative n·τⁿ⁻¹ at τ (hasDerivAt_pow), and τⁿ ≠ 0 by step 1. By the quotient rule (HasDerivAt.div), F has derivative (I₁(τ)·τⁿ − I(τ)·(n·τⁿ⁻¹))/(τⁿ)² at τ.

3. (Identifying the derivative.) We show (I₁τⁿ − I·nτⁿ⁻¹)/(τⁿ)² = D(τ), writing I, I₁, J₁, L for their values at τ. The hypothesis at τ reads nI − τI₁ + τJ₁ + L = 0.
   (a) Case n = 0. The left side is I₁, because τ⁰ = 1 and the term with factor n vanishes. The hypothesis gives τI₁ = τJ₁ + L, so I₁ = J₁ + L/τ = J₁/τ⁰ + L/τ¹ = D(τ), using τ ≠ 0.
   (b) Case n = m + 1. Then nτⁿ⁻¹ = (m+1)·τ^m, and D(τ) = (J₁·τ^{m+2} + τ^{m+1}·L)/(τ^{m+1}·τ^{m+2}). All denominators are nonzero by step 1, so cross-multiplying turns the claim into (J₁τ^{m+2} + τ^{m+1}L)·(τ^{m+1})² = (I₁τ^{m+1} − I·(m+1)τ^m)·(τ^{m+1}·τ^{m+2}). The left minus the right side equals τ^{3m+3}·((m+1)I − τI₁ + τJ₁ + L), which is 0 by the hypothesis.
   Hence F has derivative D(τ) at every τ ∈ [σ, ρ].

4. (Continuity and integrability.) On [σ, ρ], J₁ and L are continuous, and t ↦ tⁿ and t ↦ tⁿ⁺¹ are continuous and nonvanishing by step 1. So τ ↦ J₁(τ)/τⁿ, τ ↦ L(τ)/τⁿ⁺¹ and their sum D are continuous on [σ, ρ]. Consequently:
   - D is interval integrable on [σ, ρ] (ContinuousOn.intervalIntegrable_of_Icc).
   - J₁(τ)/τⁿ and L(τ)/τⁿ⁺¹ are integrable on the compact interval [σ, ρ] (ContinuousOn.integrableOn_Icc), hence on its subset (σ, ρ].

5. (Fundamental theorem of calculus.) Since σ ≤ ρ, [σ, ρ] = uIcc σ ρ. F has derivative D at every point of uIcc σ ρ by step 3, and D is interval integrable by step 4, so ∫_σ^ρ D(τ) dτ = F(ρ) − F(σ) (intervalIntegral.integral_eq_sub_of_hasDerivAt). Because σ ≤ ρ, ∫_σ^ρ D = ∫_{(σ,ρ]} D (intervalIntegral.integral_of_le).

6. (Splitting.) By step 4 both summands of D are integrable on (σ, ρ], so ∫_{(σ,ρ]} D = ∫_{(σ,ρ]} J₁(τ)/τⁿ dτ + ∫_{(σ,ρ]} L(τ)/τⁿ⁺¹ dτ (integral_add). Combining this with step 5: I(ρ)/ρⁿ − I(σ)/σⁿ = F(ρ) − F(σ) = ∫_{(σ,ρ]} J₁(τ)/τⁿ dτ + ∫_{(σ,ρ]} L(τ)/τⁿ⁺¹ dτ. ∎
